title: Show who wrote a source and why
statement: When a question rests on a primary source, show students who wrote it and why, and cite it accurately.
example: Correcting one source's citation and showing another's purpose was one of six repairs an audit required before a unit could be copied.
detail: An independent semantic audit of an AP history unit found no wrong or ambiguous key but blocked the unit from being replicated on six repair buckets. One bucket was to correct a source's citation to the right chapters and collection, and to add the reform-advocate purpose behind another source to the citation context students see. A later commit closed all six, after which the unit's validator passed with zero errors and zero warnings.

evidence.quote: no wrong or ambiguous MCQ key
chapters I, III, and V and Library of Congress General Collections
reform-advocate purpose to student-visible citation context.
closes the six repair buckets recorded in kb-0167
passed with zero errors and zero warnings

The identity of the creator, date, repository, edition, excerpt boundary, adaptation, rights basis, and content digest determine what the student is actually reading. Those facts also shape the historical interpretation.
